Thus, in biliary atresia, there are prominent histologic features, including a limited involvement of the liver acinus with very few multinucleated giant hepatocytes, which should have six or more nuclei. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (a, b, c). a: Low-power H&E of the extrahepatic bile duct showing a fibrotic cord with neurovascular hyperplasia, the classic obliterative extrahepatic ductal sclerosis of biliary atresia; the in-text explicitly calls this dense fibrotic tissue definitive anatomical evidence of BA. b: H&E of porta hepatis showing a neonatal hepatitis pattern with florid ductular proliferation (black arrows), giant cell transformation and bile pigmentation; the in-text stresses that this florid ductular reaction contrasts with the absent ductular response of isolated ALGS, supporting biliary atresia attribution. c: Liver wedge biopsy H&E showing a neonatal hepatitis pattern with only focal interlobular bile duct absence (black arrow). The in-text states the characteristic bile duct paucity of ALGS was not yet histologically definitive and that duct loss did not exceed 50% of portal tracts, so the paucity finding is not sufficient for ALGS; the panel is therefore kept...

panels.figure_caption: Histopathology: (a) extrahepatic bile duct, demonstrating a fibrotic cord with neurovascular hyperplasia (white arrows) (hematoxylin and eosin, ×2); (b) porta hepatis, displaying neonatal hepatitis pattern with giant cell transformation (green arrows) and inflammatory cell infiltration, ductular proliferation (black arrows), bile pigmentation of hepatocytes (hematoxylin and eosin, ×10); (c) liver wedge biopsy, demonstrating neonatal hepatitis pattern; focal absence of interlobular bile duct is noted (black arrow: no bile duct in this portal tract), but loss of bile duct did not exceed 50% of the portal tracts (hematoxylin and eosin, ×10); (d) liver wedge biopsy, immunostained with CK19 displaying positive expression in areas of prominent bile ductular proliferation (cytokeratin 19 immunohistochemical staining, ×4).
in_text_mentions: sia and dense fibrotic tissue, which provides definitive anatomical evidence of BA. Furthermore, a concurrent liver wedge biopsy demonstrated significant portal and lobular inflammation, marked giant cell transformation, and a florid, diffuse ductular reaction intensely highlighted by Cytokeratin 19 (CK19) immunostaining—features that directly contrast with the lack of ductular response typically seen in isolated ALGS. Interlobular bile duct loss was focal and did not exceed 50% of the portal tracts (Figure 4). The characteristic bile duct paucity of ALGS was not yet histologically definitive.
